version.changelog:
MyStock 1.1.6 - Minor update

- Added a new test script: scripts/test_batch_api.py.
- Updated backend logic and APIs in backend/main.py.
- Improved or fixed parts of the frontend in frontend/index.html.
- Documentation updated in SKILL.md to reflect latest changes and version bump.

llm.summary: This stock assistant has a coherent purpose, but it exposes and mutates private portfolio data through an unauthenticated network service and can send financial context and API keys to external AI services.

dimensions.detail: The backend binds to 0.0.0.0 with wildcard CORS and no authentication, which is overbroad for a personal local portfolio tool documented mainly as localhost access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation and startup use package-management actions, including global unpinned jsdom installation, pip upgrade behavior, and unversioned remote frontend scripts from a CDN without integrity metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructions are broad for stock analysis and investment research, but I did not find prompt hijacking directives; referenced backend and frontend files are present and inspectable.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: I found no autostart service, scheduled task, system backdoor, or OS privilege escalation, but the startup script launches long-running background servers and writes local runtime investment data in the project directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stock quotes, portfolio management, notes, shareholder activity, and AI chat features match the stated purpose, but the implementation gives unauthenticated API clients read/write access to portfolio, watchlist, history, insights, and memos, and chat can include portfolio context in provider requests.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing. Run it only on a trusted local machine or network, avoid exposing port 8000, do not configure AI keys until provider destinations and transmitted data are clear, rotate any real key used with the zhipu option, and remove bundled portfolio/memo data before use or redistribution.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: the cited backend/main.py and frontend/index.html references are ordinary development notes, and the files are present in the artifact.
[PE3] expected: API-key configuration via environment variables or a local .env file is expected for optional AI providers, but the guidance lacks adequate secret-handling warnings.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: docs suggest code-based API key configuration and do not clearly disclose that AI chat may transmit user messages, history, and portfolio/watchlist context to third-party providers.
[SC4] unexpected: Accepted as a dependency hygiene concern: the requirements include old pinned FastAPI and python-multipart versions flagged by the scanner.
[SC6] expected: Overridden: uvicorn is a normal FastAPI ASGI server dependency, not meaningful typosquatting evidence here.
[P2] expected: Overridden: inspected HTML comments are structural Chinese section labels and UI comments, not hidden instructions to the agent.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a routing-scope note: the invocation language could trigger for broad finance or investment discussion beyond specific stock-tool use.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted: backend/main.py has wildcard CORS, no authentication, read/write portfolio endpoints, memo/history/insight endpoints, and uvicorn host 0.0.0.0.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: /api/chat appends up to 20 portfolio and 20 watchlist entries to chat messages before provider calls, and ai_service.py sends API keys and chat content to hardcoded provider URLs, including an under-documented zhipu URL.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted: install/startup/browser paths can fetch mutable dependencies or scripts, including global npm installation and unversioned CDN JavaScript.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: the package includes populated portfolio_data.json and memos.json with holdings, watchlists, timestamps, and investment notes rather than sanitized example data.
